explanations.answer: Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says the finders brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). Moses is Israel's leader, and Aaron is his brother, the priest. So this wasn't a quiet word in somebody's ear. The whole crowd was standing right there.

explanations.answer: Joshua and Caleb and the elders
explanations.explanation: Good guess, friend, because those names do show up in Numbers. Joshua and Caleb are the two spies who trusted God about the land. But in this passage, the finders bring the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). No elders are named here. It's a bit like walking into the wrong bakery and asking for the owner.

explanations.answer: Eleazar and the priests at the tabernacle
explanations.explanation: Eleazar is Aaron's son, so I see why he came to mind. But the text doesn't mention him here at all. The finders brought the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). The tabernacle isn't mentioned in this part of the story either, so I'd keep it out of the picture.

Right on the money, baker. The text says that because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). Nobody guessed and nobody rushed. They waited to be told. It's the opposite of me eyeballing a recipe, and I've got the burnt batches to prove it.

I get the thought, friend, but the text goes another way. It says they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). Nobody had said what should be done to him yet, so they kept him there instead of letting him walk off. Release would have left the question hanging.

Banish sounds like a decision, and that's the catch. The text says it had not been declared what should be done to him, so they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). No one sent him away or picked a punishment on their own. They held him and waited for word.

explanations.answer: He must be put to death
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker, and it's a heavy one. The LORD tells Moses, "The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp." (Numbers 15:35) That's the answer the people had been waiting for. It's a hard line to read, and I won't pretend otherwise.

explanations.answer: He must bring a sin offering
explanations.explanation: Sin offerings do come up just before this in Numbers 15, but that's not what the LORD says here. He tells Moses, "The man must surely be put to death." (Numbers 15:35) The answer was given right to Moses, plain and short. It's a heavy moment, so no dancing around it.

explanations.answer: He must pay back the wood he took
explanations.explanation: Paying back wood would be a tidy fix, friend, but the text never mentions anything like it. The LORD tells Moses, "The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp." (Numbers 15:35) It's a hard answer to read, and I think it's okay to feel that.

Tassels it is, baker. God tells them to make tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel (Numbers 15:38). That's a small thing to wear, but it sits right there on every corner. I'd still lose mine in the dough by lunchtime.

Bells are a fair guess, friend, and I think of my cookie cutter kid Ruby, the bell, every time. But for the garments in this passage, God says tassels for the corners, with a blue cord on each one (Numbers 15:38). Nothing here says bells. The only jingling in my bakery is the timer.

Pomegranates are a real thing on some clothing in the Bible, but they're not what God asks for here. He tells the Israelites to make tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel (Numbers 15:38). Keep it simple, friend: corners, tassels, blue cord.

That's it, baker. God says the tassels are "…for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD…" (Numbers 15:39). One glance down and there's the reminder. It works like a string around my finger, except mine always ends up in the cookie dough.

That would be a long list to hang on one tassel, friend. God doesn't say anything about ancestors here. He says the tassels are "…for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD…" (Numbers 15:39). The tassel points to what God commanded.

explanations.answer: all of the places they camped
explanations.explanation: I love a good travel memory, baker, but that's not the point of the tassels. God says they're "…for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD…" (Numbers 15:39). Their campsites aren't mentioned. The tassel is there to bring His commandments to mind.

Careful, friend, this one flips the verse around. God says the tassels are so they may remember His commandments and obey them "…and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes." (Numbers 15:39) So the tassels aren't there to help them follow their own heart and eyes. They're there to keep them from it.

Yes, baker, you caught it. God says the tassels are so they may remember the commandments of the LORD and obey them, "…and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes." (Numbers 15:39) The tassels point away from following their own heart and eyes, not toward it. It's a tricky one, and you didn't flinch.

Word for word, baker. God says, "Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God." (Numbers 15:40) Remembering and obeying go together in that line, and the result is being holy to Him. That's a quote worth keeping on the counter.

I can see why it might sound too neat, friend, but it's exactly what the text says. God says, "Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God." (Numbers 15:40) Every word is right there in the verse. So True was the way to go.

Egypt, baker, right on target. God says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) He's reminding them who He is and what He did for them. That's a good thing to hear before you head back to the oven.

Moab is a real place, friend, a land east of the Dead Sea. But God doesn't name it here. He says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) The land He brought them out of was Egypt.

Edom is another real place in the Bible, a land south of the Dead Sea. But it's not the one God names here. He says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) Egypt is the answer, and you'll get it next time.
